title: Idempotent completeness of the common-stage Weil category
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ with
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and let
$D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ be the common-stage Weil category of
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Then $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ is idempotent
complete, and the canonical functor

$$
 D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)\longrightarrow
 \Kar\bigl(D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)\bigr)
$$

into its Karoubi envelope is an equivalence.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C=D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ and $T=Lg_Y^*$, so that the Weil category is the category of pairs $(K,\theta:TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The scheme $Y$ is finite type over $k$: a finite affine cover of $Y_0$ by spectra of finitely generated $k_0$-algebras base changes to a finite affine cover of $Y$ by their tensor products with $k$, generated over $k$ by the images of the same generators [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Therefore [lem-weil-qbar-idempotent-complete] applies and $\mathcal C$ is idempotent complete. For any idempotent $e$ on a Weil pair $(K,\theta)$, its underlying endomorphism satisfies $e^2=e$ and $e\theta=\theta T(e)$. Choose in $\mathcal C$ a splitting $i:L\to K$, $r:K\to L$, with $ri=1_L$ and $ir=e$. In particular $ei=i$ and $re=r$.

source.place: Replacement for the first sentence and finite-stage reduction: use the underlying common-stage category and its existing idempotent-completeness theorem.

proof.text: The category of Weil pairs is additive. Indeed the pullback $T$ is additive by its morphism formulas in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]: the rational-stage formulas extend additively and the common-stage formulas apply these maps conjugated by comparison isomorphisms. Thus $u\theta=\theta'T(u)$ cuts out an abelian subgroup of each underlying Hom group [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The zero object has its unique structure isomorphism, and the biproduct of $(K,\theta)$ and $(K',\theta')$ has underlying object $K\oplus K'$ and structure $T(K\oplus K')\cong TK\oplus TK'\xrightarrow{\theta\oplus\theta'}K\oplus K'$. The usual inclusions and projections commute with these structure maps, so their biproduct identities hold also for pairs.

source.place: Correction of the claimed triangulated structure: only the additive structure follows directly from the reviewed fixed-pair definition.

proof.text:
Give $L$ the structure map $\theta_L=r\theta T(i):TL\to L$. Its inverse is $\psi=T(r)\theta^{-1}i:L\to TL$, since functoriality and $e\theta=\theta T(e)$ give
$$
\theta_L\psi=r\theta T(ir)\theta^{-1}i=r e i=1_L,
\qquad
\psi\theta_L=T(r)\theta^{-1}e\theta T(i)=T(r e i)=1_{TL}.
$$
Hence $(L,\theta_L)$ is a Weil pair by [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The two splitting maps are Weil morphisms because
$$
i\theta_L=e\theta T(i)=\theta T(ei)=\theta T(i),
\qquad
\theta_LT(r)=r\theta T(e)=r e\theta=r\theta.
$$
Their composites remain $ri=1$ and $ir=e$ in the category of pairs, whose composition and identities are those of $\mathcal C$. Thus every idempotent of the Weil category splits.

source.place: Replacement for the claimed equivariant bounded-t-structure argument: explicit Frobenius structure on the retract.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal W=D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$. For an object $(X,e)$ of $\Kar(\mathcal W)$, choose a splitting $i:L\to X$, $r:X\to L$ in $\mathcal W$ as above. By [def-weil-karoubi-envelope], $i$ and $r$ are morphisms $(L,1_L)\to(X,e)$ and $(X,e)\to(L,1_L)$, since $ei=i$ and $re=r$. Their composites are $1_L$ and $e$, respectively, which are exactly the two identities in the envelope. Every object of the envelope is therefore isomorphic to the image of an object of $\mathcal W$. Full faithfulness is [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-fully-faithful], so the canonical functor is an equivalence. Its action on morphisms is the identity, hence it is additive for the inherited Hom-group structures.

source.place: Last clause: full faithfulness and explicit essential surjectivity; exactness removed because the fixed-pair definition supplies no triangulation.

proof_origin.place: Correction of the derived-of-Weil-sheaves identification; explicit splitting in fixed pairs and the Karoubi construction.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: exact equivalence presupposes a triangulated structure, but the reviewed definition is a fixed-pair category and explicitly disclaims such a structure. Removed only exact, retaining all hypotheses and both categorical conclusions; the equivalence is also additive. Replaced the incorrect derived-of-Weil-sheaves identification by an explicit Frobenius structure on a splitting of the underlying idempotent. The only non-elementary input is the existing common-stage coefficient idempotent-completeness lemma. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Current main-20261015 proof is unchanged from the imported proof and incorrectly identifies fixed pairs with a derived category of Weil sheaves. Steps 1 and 3 replace that false inference; step 2 establishes additivity and step 4 proves the final Karoubi equivalence. This is a correction below the unit level: sk-def-purity-conv is a conventions remark with no proof steps; its statement and the chapter route are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Provides idempotent completeness of the underlying common-stage coefficient category, a generic tool for lifting a splitting to a Frobenius-fixed pair. The conventions unit states no such theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q16-48981e064 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its four steps, the master and main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof, every cited node's statement, the unit sk-def-purity-conv (no proof steps) and the one DAG citer. Statement: the only change is dropping 'exact'. This is justified and not a target weakening. def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex defines a fixed-pair category and says no triangulated structure is part of it, so 'exact equivalence' has no meaning there. The Jordan-block example at Spec k_0 (a nonsplit equivariant extension, while Hom of pairs into Lambda[1] is zero) shows the blueprint proof wrongly identifies fixed pairs with D^b of Weil sheaves. That is a source error the maintainer should record in HUMAN.md; the report names it under 'Statement corrected' rather than the E7 heading '## Source error'. The item is not a GOAL target. Its only citer, prop-pod-dual-tate-data-compatibility, uses only idempotent splitting, which is kept. Step 1: Y is finite type over k, elementary from def-weil-finite-type-morphism. lem-weil-qbar-idempotent-complete needs exactly a finite-type k-scheme and l != p, and its C_Y is the same category as D^b_c(Y,Qlb); it gives only the underlying splitting. A DFS over all dependencies of the cited nodes finds no cycle. Step 2: Lg* is additive (linear rational-level formula, and at the common stage it is conjugated by comparison isomorphisms); the morphism condition cuts out subgroups and the biproduct structure is correct. Step 3: I checked by hand that theta_L psi = rei = 1, psi theta_L = T(rei) = 1, i theta_L = theta T(i) and theta_L T(r) = r theta, using e theta = theta T(e). Step 4: i = e i 1 and r = 1 r e are Karoubi morphisms with composites 1_L and e, which gives essential surjectivity; full faithfulness is the cited node, applied to the additive category from step 2. Small cases e=0, e=1, empty Y_0, a block-diagonal theta and a swap-stable diagonal summand all work. There are no new nodes. A DAG-wide scan for idempotent plus Weil or fixed-pair statements found no duplicate (prop-trf-karoubi-independence is unrelated). Accepted tool_use: lem-weil-qbar-idempotent-complete (unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general), used as a black-box idempotent completeness of the coefficient category; the blueprint route also left the unit here.
